mainTopic: Impurity and eating מעשר and תרומה, then the scope of פיגול: which items have מתירין, and whose view includes the מצורע's oil
overview: The עמוד opens by challenging a reading of a ברייתא about eating מעשר and תרומה while impure. Because of the rule of דיו, a קל וחומר could never have led us to a death penalty. זעירי answers that 'lenient' means טומאת שרץ and 'stringent' means טומאת מת. The Torah mentioned טומאת מת so we would not think it brings death for eating מעשר. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that anything with מתירין can become פיגול. A ברייתא widens פיגול step by step from שלמים to every holy item, using a chain of word-links from טומאה to נותר to פיגול. It then uses שלמים as the model: only items that something else permits can become פיגול. רבי שמעון narrows this to items whose מתיר is on the outer מזבח. The גמרא then asks whose view the ברייתא follows. רבי מאיר fits its inclusion of the מצורע's oil but not its ending. רב יוסף answers that it follows רבי, for whom the oil's own sprinklings permit it and can make it פיגול. The עמוד ends with רבי ירמיה shocked at רב יוסף's answer, and his reason comes on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Without the stringent case, would we really have guessed death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the reading of the ברייתא. Without the חמורות case, we would have learned it from טומאת שרץ through a קל וחומר, and דיו would limit it to a לאו, not death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the stringent case had not been stated, would I really have said that the stringent case carries death? It would come from the impurity of a שרץ, and the rule of דיו says a conclusion can be no stronger than its source!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the ברייתא's claim that, without the extra words, we would have mistakenly given the stringent case a death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stringent case were missing, we would learn it from the lighter case of טומאת שרץ with a קל וחומר. The rule of דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון says a learned law can never be harsher than its source. Since the source only carries a לאו, we could never reach death, so the ברייתא's 'mistake' could not have happened.

keyTerms.meaning: the stringent cases
impurity from a dead creeping creature
death at the hand of Heaven

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: a law learned by קל וחומר is only as strong as its source

steps.confusionAlert: The question mark here is a challenge, not a real question. The גמרא is saying, 'You could never have thought that!'

would I have said that for the stringent cases it is death?!
But it would come from the impurity of a שרץ,
phrases.notes: He means we would learn it through a קל וחומר from the lighter case of a שרץ.

phrases.english: and it is enough for what comes from the inference
to be like its source!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ חֲמוּרוֹת, הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier reading of the ברייתא from the previous עמוד
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that without חמורות we would have assigned death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from טומאת שרץ is capped by דיו, so it could never produce death

steps.title: זעירי redefines the lenient and stringent cases
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that קלות means טומאת שרץ and חמורות means טומאת מת. If only טומאת שרץ had been stated, a person impure from a שרץ would get a לאו for eating מעשר and death for eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: 'Lenient' means the impurity of a שרץ, and 'stringent' means the impurity of a dead body. This is what the ברייתא means: If the impurity of a שרץ had been stated, and מעשר and תרומה were stated, but the impurity of a dead body was not stated, I would have said: the lenient impurity eating lenient food is a לאו, and eating stringent food is death.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי answers the challenge by giving new meanings to the words 'lenient' and 'stringent' in the ברייתא. He then starts laying out what we would have thought without the extra verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words now describe two levels of impurity (שרץ and מת), not two penalties learned from each other. So no קל וחומר with דיו is involved. Within טומאת שרץ itself, the known rules are a לאו for מעשר and death for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: the lenient cases
impurity from a dead body, the most severe type
second tithe, a food with lighter rules
the כהן's portion, a food with stricter rules
a negative commandment, punished by lashes

phrases.english: זעירי said:
'Lenient' means the impurity of a שרץ,
'stringent' means the impurity of a dead body.
And this is what the ברייתא is saying:
If the impurity of a שרץ had been stated
and מעשר and תרומה had been stated,
but the impurity of a dead body had not been stated –
I would have said: the lenient impurity on the lenient food is a לאו,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording: the lenient impurity (שרץ) on the lenient food (מעשר).

phrases.english: and on the stringent food it is death;
phrases.notes: The stringent food here is תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by reinterpreting the ברייתא's terms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קלות and חמורות describe penalties learned from each other through a קל וחומר
steps.terutzMaskana: קלות means טומאת שרץ and חמורות means טומאת מת, so no דיו problem arises

steps.title: Why the Torah had to mention טומאת מת
steps.stepSummary: Because a שרץ-impure person eating תרומה gets death, we might have said a מת-impure person eating מעשר also gets death. So the Torah mentioned טומאת מת to teach that it is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the lenient impurity eating stringent food is death, the stringent impurity eating lenient food would also be death. That is why the stringent case was stated.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי finishes his explanation by showing what mistake the Torah's mention of טומאת מת prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea crosses the cases: light impurity with strict food is death, so strict impurity with light food should also be death. By stating טומאת מת in connection with מעשר, the Torah shows that even this severe impurity brings only a לאו for מעשר. This explains the ברייתא's line 'לכך נאמרו חמורות' without any דיו problem.

keyTerms.meaning: that is why it was stated
also

steps.whatToRemember: According to זעירי, טומאת מת was stated so we would not think it brings death for eating מעשר. Eating מעשר while impure is only a לאו, no matter how severe the impurity.

phrases.english: And since the lenient impurity on the stringent food is death –
the stringent impurity on the lenient food would also be death;
phrases.notes: A person impure from a dead body who eats מעשר.

phrases.english: therefore the stringent case was stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes זעירי's answer begun in step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the verse, a person impure from a מת who eats מעשר would get death
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאת מת was stated to limit eating מעשר in that state to a לאו

steps.title: The משנה: anything with מתירין can become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה to begin a new section: anything that has מתירין, whether for a person or for the מזבח, makes one liable for eating it as פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that has permitting factors, whether for a person or for the altar, one is liable for it because of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתירין are the parts of the service that make an offering allowed, such as the sprinkling of the blood. The rule is that פיגול only applies to things that have such a permitting step. This holds whether the step permits the meat for people or permits burning on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: permitting factors, the service that makes an offering allowed
an offering ruined by a wrong intention about its time, and forbidden to eat
the altar
one is liable to punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets the boundary of פיגול. Only items that have a permitting step can become פיגול, and the following גמרא builds on it.

phrases.english: Anything that has permitting factors,
whether for a person or for the altar –
one is liable for it because of פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין, בֵּין לְאָדָם בֵּין לְמִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section; not connected to the טומאה discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything with מתירין, for a person or for the מזבח, makes one liable for פיגול

steps.title: The ברייתא suggests פיגול might apply only to offerings like peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא raises the idea that פיגול applies only to offerings that are eaten for two days and one night, like שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Or maybe the verse includes only offerings similar to peace offerings. Just as peace offerings are special in that they are eaten for two days and one night, so too, only offerings eaten for two days and one night can become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain the משנה's rule that anything with מתירין can become פיגול. The ברייתא opens with a narrow idea that it will widen in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about פיגול is written about שלמים, so one might think the law covers only offerings that share the special feature of שלמים: they are eaten for two days and one night. This narrow starting point sets up the questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings, eaten for two days and the night between them
An offering made unfit by the intent to eat or burn it after its proper time
Something similar to it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Or perhaps it includes
only what is similar to peace offerings;
just as peace offerings are special
in that they are eaten for two days and one night,
so too, anything that is eaten
for two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אוֹ אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶלָּא כַּיּוֹצֵא בִּשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the source for the משנה quoted in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First idea (to be widened): פיגול applies only to offerings eaten for two days and one night, like שלמים.

steps.title: What about offerings eaten for only one day and a night?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that offerings eaten for a shorter time can also become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that an offering eaten for only one day and a night can also become פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to begin widening the law. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many offerings are eaten for a shorter time than שלמים: only the day they are brought and the night after. Under the narrow idea from step 5 they would be left out, so the ברייתא looks for a source that includes them.

keyTerms.meaning: Eaten for one day and the following night, for example a חַטָּאת or אָשָׁם
From where do we know?
Sin offering, an example of an offering eaten for a day and a night

phrases.english: An offering eaten for one day and a night — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the narrow limit set in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that includes offerings eaten for only one day and a night

steps.title: The word 'מבשר' includes any offering whose leftover meat is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מבשר' (of the flesh) widens פיגול to every offering whose remaining meat is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'Of the flesh.' This teaches that any offering whose leftovers are eaten can become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 6 with the word 'מבשר' from the פיגול verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have just said 'if any of his peace offering is eaten.' The extra word 'מבשר' shifts the focus to the meat itself, so whether the meat is eaten for two days or one day does not matter. As long as the meat left over after the מזבח parts are burned gets eaten, the offering is included.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; it introduces the source
'Of the flesh,' a word in the פיגול verse
Its leftovers, meaning the meat remaining after the מזבח portions are burned

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Of the flesh' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18

phrases.english: anything whose leftovers are eaten.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מבשר' includes every offering whose remaining meat is eaten, even if only for a day and a night.

steps.title: What about an עולה, whose meat is not eaten at all?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know an עולה can become פיגול, since none of its meat is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עולה, whose leftovers are not eaten — from where do we know it can become פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes further and asks about an offering that the answer in step 7 does not cover. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 included offerings whose meat is eaten. An עולה is burned completely on the מזבח and nothing is eaten, so 'מבשר' cannot include it. A new source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Its leftovers are not eaten

phrases.english: A burnt offering, whose leftovers are not eaten — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points to a case left out by the answer in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that includes an עולה in פיגול

steps.title: The word 'זבח' includes the עולה
steps.stepSummary: The word 'זבח' (sacrifice) includes every slaughtered offering, even an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'sacrifice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 8 with the word 'זבח' from the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זבח' describes any animal that is slaughtered as an offering. Being slaughtered, not having its meat eaten, is what counts here, so an עולה is included.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughtered offering
Slaughter, which every זבח has

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Sacrifice.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זבח' includes all slaughtered offerings, including an עולה.

steps.title: What about birds, מנחות, and even the מצורע's oil?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how to include items that are not slaughtered at all, all the way down to the לוג שמן of a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include bird offerings and meal offerings, until I even include the לוג of oil of a מצורע?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about items that the word 'זבח' cannot cover. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds are not slaughtered normally (they get מליקה), and מנחות and oil are not animals at all. Since 'זבח' means a slaughtered animal, these need yet another source. The ברייתא wants to go as far as the לוג שמן of a מצורע, which also has a מתיר (what exactly permits it is discussed later in the עמוד).

keyTerms.meaning: Bird offerings
Meal offerings made of flour
The measure of oil brought with the guilt offering of a healed מצורע
To include

phrases.english: From where do we know to include
bird offerings and meal offerings,
until I even include
the log of oil of a leper?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points to items left out by the word 'זבח' in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that includes non-slaughtered items (birds, מנחות, oil) in פיגול

steps.title: 'Which they consecrate to Me' includes everything sacred
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'אשר הם מקדישים לי' covers every consecrated item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse states: 'Which they consecrate to Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 10 with a verse that speaks broadly about anything made holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase is not limited to animals or slaughtered offerings. It covers anything consecrated, so birds, מנחות, and the מצורע's oil are all included.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Which they consecrate to Me,' a verse covering all holy items
Consecrated items

steps.confusionAlert: This verse is from the section about eating sacred food while טמא. It is not a verse about פיגול. The next step explains how it gets carried over to פיגול.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'Which they consecrate to Me.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The broad phrase 'אשר הם מקדישים לי' includes every consecrated item.

steps.title: The chain from טומאה to נותר to פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Two גזירות שוות bring the broad scope of the טומאה verse over to נותר, and then from נותר to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: נותר is learned from טומאה through the shared word 'profaning,' and פיגול is learned from נותר through the shared word 'iniquity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how a verse about טומאה can teach a law about פיגול: by a chain of two word-links.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חילול' (profaning) appears both by טומאה and by נותר, so נותר applies to everything טומאה applies to. Then the word 'עון' (iniquity) appears both by נותר and by פיגול, so פיגול gets the same wide range. In the end every consecrated item, down to the מצורע's oil, can become פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial food left past its time
Ritual impurity, here eating sacred food while טמא
Learning one law from another through a shared word
Profaning
Iniquity

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול covers everything with מתירין, step by step: 'מבשר' (eaten offerings), 'זבח' (עולה), 'אשר הם מקדישים לי' (birds, מנחות, oil). That last verse reaches פיגול through טומאה → נותר → פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the full source for the משנה's rule from step 4 that anything with מתירין, for a person or for the מזבח, makes one liable for פיגול.

phrases.english: And נותר is derived
'profaning'–'profaning' from impurity,
phrases.notes: 'Profaning' appears by נותר (ויקרא 19:8) and by טומאה (ויקרא 22:2).

phrases.english: and פיגול is derived
'iniquity'–'iniquity' from נותר.
phrases.notes: 'Iniquity' appears by פיגול (ויקרא 7:18) and by נותר (ויקרא 19:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the טומאה verse from step 11 applies to פיגול
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through חילול-חילול (טומאה to נותר) and עון-עון (נותר to פיגול), פיגול applies to every consecrated item that has מתירין.

steps.title: If everything is included, why does the verse mention peace offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פיגול verse mentions שלמים when the law already covers every consecrated item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since in the end the verse includes everything, why does it say 'peace offerings' at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question about the wording of the פסוק. It is setting up the next step, which uses the word שלמים to teach a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the scope of פיגול was stretched to cover every consecrated item. If so, the word שלמים in the פסוק seems to add nothing. The ברייתא assumes no word in the תורה is extra, so the mention of שלמים must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings; the offering the פיגול verse talks about
To include
Now, given what we have said

phrases.english: And since in the end it includes every item,
phrases.notes: This points back to step 12, where the verse was shown to include everything, even the לוג שמן of a מצורע.

phrases.english: why, now, does it say 'peace offerings'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל דָּבָר, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the verse names שלמים, given the broad inclusion just derived
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the specific mention of שלמים in the פיגול verse teach?

steps.title: Peace offerings are the model: only items with a permitting factor
steps.stepSummary: Like שלמים, an item can become פיגול only if something else makes it permitted, either for a person or for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: To teach you: just as peace offerings have something that permits them, either to a person or to the altar, so anything that has something permitting it, to a person or to the altar, can bring liability for פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that שלמים are mentioned to set a pattern. An item can become פיגול only if it has a מתיר, something else that makes it permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of שלמים permits the meat to be eaten and the fats to be burned on the מזבח. So the word שלמים narrows the broad inclusion from step 12. Only items that have a מתיר like this can become פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitting factors; the service, such as the blood, that makes the rest of the offering allowed
Special, marked out by a certain feature
An offering made invalid by the intent to eat or burn it at the wrong time
Just as ... so too; the form of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: The rule from שלמים: something can become פיגול only if it has a מתיר, either for a person or for the מזבח.

phrases.english: To tell you:
just as peace offerings are special
in that they have permitting factors,
phrases.notes: The blood of the שלמים is what permits the rest of the animal.

phrases.english: whether for a person or for the altar,
so too anything that has permitting factors,
whether for a person or for the altar,
one is liable for them because of פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by turning שלמים into a model that limits the scope
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שלמים teach that only items with a מתיר, for a person or for the מזבח, are subject to פיגול.

steps.title: Examples of offerings whose blood permits other parts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists offerings that fit the rule because their blood permits something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The burnt offering: its blood permits its meat for the altar and its hide for the priests. The bird burnt offering: its blood permits its meat for the altar. The bird sin offering: its blood permits its meat for the priests. The burned bulls and burned goats: their blood permits their fats to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now shows which offerings fit the rule from step 14. In each case, the blood is the מתיר for some other part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example shows a different kind of permitting. Some permit for the מזבח (the עולה meat, the עולת העוף, the אימורים of the burned bulls and goats). Some permit for people (the עולה hide and the חטאת העוף meat for the כהנים). Since every one of them has a מתיר, every one of them can become פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a burnt offering
A bird brought as a sin offering
Bulls whose meat is burned outside the camp
Goats whose meat is burned outside the camp
The fats and parts burned on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹלָה – דָּמָהּ מַתִּיר אֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: The burnt offering: its blood permits its meat for the altar,
and its hide for the priests.
The bird burnt offering: its blood permits
its meat for the altar.
The bird sin offering: its blood permits
its meat for the priests.
Burned bulls and burned goats:
their blood permits their fats to be offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹלָה – דָּמָהּ מַתִּיר אֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 14 to specific offerings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולה, עולת העוף, חטאת העוף, and the burned bulls and goats all have a מתיר, so they can become פיגול.

steps.title: Items left out because nothing else permits them
steps.stepSummary: The rule from שלמים leaves out the קומץ, the frankincense, the incense, several kinds of מנחות, and the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I exclude the handful, the frankincense, the incense, the priests' meal offering, the anointed priest's meal offering, the libation meal offering, and the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא lists items that do not fit the rule from step 14. These items cannot become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these items has something else that permits it. Some are themselves the מתיר, like the קומץ and the blood. Others are burned completely with nothing to permit them, like the incense and the מנחות of כהנים. Since they have no מתיר, the comparison to שלמים leaves them out.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense
The incense
The anointed כהן גדול
The meal offering brought with the wine libations

steps.confusionAlert: The קומץ and the blood are left out here, meaning one is not liable for פיגול for eating them. They are still what makes other things פיגול, because they are the מתירין.

phrases.english: And I exclude the handful,
and the frankincense, and the incense,
and the priests' meal offering, and the anointed priest's meal offering,
and the libation meal offering, and the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the rule: items with no מתיר are left out
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items that have no מתיר of their own are not subject to פיגול.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the permitting factor must be on the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads the שלמים comparison more narrowly. Only items whose מתיר is placed on the outer מזבח are subject to פיגול, so the burned bulls and goats are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: just as peace offerings have their permitting factor on the outer altar, and one is liable for them, so anything with its permitting factor on the outer altar brings liability for פיגול. This leaves out the burned bulls and burned goats. Since their blood is not placed on the outer altar like peace offerings, one is not liable for them because of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון learns a different detail from שלמים: where the מתיר is placed. Because of this, he leaves out the burned bulls and goats, which the first opinion had included in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of שלמים is placed on the outer מזבח. The blood of the burned bulls and goats is placed inside the היכל. So for רבי שמעון they are not like שלמים, and they cannot become פיגול. This directly argues with the first opinion's list in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer altar in the courtyard
Are left out, excluded
Since, because

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion: anything with a מתיר can become פיגול. רבי שמעון: only if the מתיר is placed on the outer מזבח, so the burned bulls and goats are left out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a disagreement about the burned bulls and goats, which the sugya can now discuss.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
just as peace offerings are special
in that their permitting factor is on the outer altar,
phrases.notes: He means the blood of the שלמים, which is placed on the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: and one is liable for it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָן עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן –
phrases.english: so too anything whose permitting factor is on the outer altar,
one is liable for it because of פיגול.
This leaves out burned bulls and burned goats,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל שֶׁאֵין עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים –
phrases.english: since their blood is not on the outer altar like peace offerings,
one is not liable for them because of פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מָה שְׁלָמִים מְיוּחָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a narrower reading of the שלמים comparison and disputes the inclusion of the burned bulls and goats in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only items whose מתיר is offered on the outer מזבח are subject to פיגול. The burned bulls and goats are left out.

steps.title: What does 'similar to peace offerings' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's phrase 'similar to שלמים' and asks which offering it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Something similar to שלמים.' What offering is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase from the ברייתא and asks what it refers to. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said פיגול applies to something 'similar to שלמים'. That must be an offering that is not itself a שלמים but is like one. The גמרא wants to know which offering that is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master', a respectful way to refer to the teacher of a quoted text
Something similar to שלמים
What is it?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. 'The Master' is the ברייתא we've just been learning.

phrases.english: Something similar to peace offerings.
What is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר כַּיּוֹצֵא בִּשְׁלָמִים מַאי נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a phrase in the ברייתא discussed in the earlier steps
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offering the ברייתא means by 'similar to שלמים'

steps.title: It is the firstborn offering
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the בכור, which is eaten for two days and one night, the same as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a בכור, which is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'similar to שלמים' means the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור and שלמים share the same eating time: two days and the night between them. That shared detail is what makes the בכור 'similar' to שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn animal brought as an offering
For two days and one night, the eating time of שלמים

phrases.english: A firstborn offering, which is eaten
for two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוֹר דְּנֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור, because it is eaten for the same time as שלמים

steps.title: A simple comparison to peace offerings fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the בכור is included. A comparison (במה מצינו) can be knocked down, because שלמים have features a בכור does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: By what method is the בכור included? If by a comparison, it can be refuted: שלמים are special, because they need סמיכה, נסכים, and waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what method teaches that a בכור is included, and shows that the obvious method, a comparison, does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A במה מצינו says: two things share one feature, so they share the law. But that can be refuted if the source has its own special features. שלמים need סמיכה, נסכים and תנופה, and a בכור needs none of them. So perhaps פיגול applies only to an offering as 'strong' as שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison: what we find in one case applies to a similar case
It can be refuted
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head
Libations of wine brought with the offering
Waving of the breast and thigh

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not doubt that a בכור can become פיגול. It only rejects one way of proving it.

phrases.english: By what method does it come?
If by 'what do we find' (a comparison),
it can be refuted:
What about peace offerings?
They require leaning of hands and libations,
and waving of the breast and thigh!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אָתֵי אִי בְּמָה מָצִינוּ אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the answer of step 19 is learned
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the בכור from שלמים by a simple comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמים have special features (סמיכה, נסכים, תנופה) that a בכור lacks, so the comparison breaks down

steps.title: Learn it from the wording 'אם האכל יאכל'
steps.stepSummary: Instead of a comparison, the בכור is included from the פסוק's wording 'אם האכל יאכל', read as a generalization and a detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is learned from 'And if any be at all eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the בכור is learned from the wording of the פסוק itself, not from a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אם' and 'האכל יאכל' are general, and 'מבשר זבח שלמיו' is a specific detail. By the method of כלל ופרט וכלל, we include anything similar to the detail. The בכור is similar to שלמים in its eating time, so it is included, and the special features of שלמים no longer matter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if any be at all eaten' (ויקרא 7:18), the פיגול verse
A generalization, a detail, and a generalization: include things similar to the detail

phrases.english: Rather,
from 'And if any be at all eaten.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:18. 'And if' and 'be at all eaten' are treated as general words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison of step 20 with a reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switches to a different method of derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור is learned from שלמים by comparison
steps.terutzMaskana: The בכור is included through כלל ופרט וכלל in the פיגול verse

steps.title: The two generalizations are side by side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two general words stand next to each other, so the order is not 'generalization, detail, generalization'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are two generalizations right next to each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 21: the פסוק's order does not fit the method being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For כלל ופרט וכלל the detail has to come between the two generalizations. Here 'אם' and 'האכל יאכל' come one after the other, and the detail comes after both. So the method seems not to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Two generalizations
That are next to each other

phrases.english: These are two generalizations
that are next to each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תְּרֵי כְּלָלֵי דִּסְמִיכִי אַהֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method proposed in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: Using כלל ופרט וכלל on 'אם האכל יאכל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The detail does not sit between the two generalizations, so the order needed for the method is missing

steps.title: רבא: move the detail between the generalizations
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the rule from ארץ ישראל: when two generalizations are next to each other, place the detail between them and read them as כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, as they say in ארץ ישראל: whenever you find two generalizations next to each other, put the detail between them and interpret them as a generalization and a detail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the objection with a rule from ארץ ישראל that allows the method even when the two generalizations are side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We may treat the later detail as if it stood between the two generalizations. Then the פסוק reads as a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, and the בכור is included because it is similar to שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the West', meaning ארץ ישראל
Cast the detail between them
Generalization and detail, a method of reading the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The בכור can become פיגול. It is learned not from a comparison to שלמים, but from the פיגול verse read as a generalization and a detail, with the detail moved between the two general words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule from ארץ ישראל lets the method of כלל ופרט וכלל work even when the פסוק does not list things in the usual order.

phrases.english: Rava said,
as they say in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: Any place that you find
two generalizations next to each other,
cast a detail between them
and interpret them as a generalization and a detail.
phrases.notes: This leads back to the full pattern from step 21: generalization, detail, generalization.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a general rule of interpretation that fits the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two side-by-side generalizations block the method of כלל ופרט וכלל
steps.terutzMaskana: Place the detail between them and read the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל

steps.title: Whose view includes the leper's oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that even the לוג שמן של מצורע is included in פיגול, and asks whose opinion that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: 'Until I include the לוג of oil of a מצורע.' Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's next line, which includes the leper's oil in the laws of פיגול. It asks which תנא holds this. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that the leper's oil can become פיגול. So the גמרא wants to know whose opinion the ברייתא follows. The answer will matter once we compare this line to the end of the same ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The measure of oil a healed leper brings along with his אשם
I include (this case in the rule)
Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: Until I include
the log of oil of a leper.
Whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from deriving the rule to identifying who holds the ברייתא's specific inclusion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the leper's oil is subject to פיגול.

steps.title: It follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who rules that one is liable for פיגול on the leper's oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר. As a ברייתא teaches: for the leper's לוג of oil, one is liable because of פיגול. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this line follows רבי מאיר. It proves this from another ברייתא where רבי מאיר says the leper's oil can become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says one is liable for פיגול on the leper's oil. That matches the ברייתא's inclusion of the oil. So the first part of the ברייתא fits רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by intending to eat it or burn it after its proper time

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir,
as it is taught in a baraita:
The log of oil of a leper:
one is liable for it because of piggul,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inclusion of the leper's oil follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא matches the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא leaves out the מנחת נסכים. That fits the רבנן, not רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last part: 'And I leave out the מנחת נסכים and the blood.' Now we have come to the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The last part of the same ברייתא seems to follow the רבנן, so the ברייתא would be split between two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first part is רבי מאיר, the whole ברייתא should be רבי מאיר. But the ending says the libations' flour offering cannot become פיגול, and רבי מאיר disagrees with that. So the beginning and the end seem to follow opposite opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (of the same source)
The flour offering brought with the libations of an animal offering
We have come to the view of the רבנן

phrases.english: Say the last part:
and I leave out the meal offering of libations
and the blood:
phrases.notes: These are left out of פיגול in the ברייתא, because nothing else makes them permitted.

phrases.english: we have come to the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 25's identification by pointing to the end of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר holds that libations can become פיגול. The ברייתא's ending leaves them out, so the ending follows the רבנן and the ברייתא would be split.

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds libations can become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר holds libations are subject to פיגול, because the animal's blood permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: for an animal's libations, one is liable because of פיגול, since the blood of the offering permits them to be offered. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof for its challenge: רבי מאיר says libations can become פיגול. So the ending of the ברייתא cannot be his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item can only become פיגול if something else makes it permitted. רבי מאיר says the animal's blood is what permits the libations, so they can become פיגול. That directly clashes with the ending of our ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The libations (flour, oil, wine) brought with an animal offering
Makes them permitted
To be offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: The libations of an animal offering:
one is liable for them because of piggul,
because the blood of the offering
permits them to be offered.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge of step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That the ending of the ברייתא cannot follow רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבי מאיר makes libations subject to פיגול

steps.title: The רבנן object: libations can come days later
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן argue that the blood cannot permit the libations, since libations may be brought up to ten days after the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But a person may bring his offerings today and the libations anytime over the next ten days!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, the רבנן challenge רבי מאיר. This shows that the רבנן disagree with him about libations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If libations can be brought days after the animal, then the animal's blood clearly does not permit them. In that case, the libations should not be able to become פיגול. This is the רבנן's view, and the ending of our ברייתא matches it.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
His animal offerings

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אָדָם מֵבִיא אֶת זְבָחָיו הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: But a person brings his offerings today,
and the libations from now until ten days!
phrases.notes: He means the libations can be brought even ten days later, apart from the animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא אָדָם מֵבִיא אֶת זְבָחָיו הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבנן attack רבי מאיר's ruling quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's claim that the blood permits the libations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Libations may be brought separately, days later, so the blood cannot be what permits them.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: only libations brought with the offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that he only meant libations brought together with the animal offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too only spoke about libations that come together with the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר limits his ruling. The blood permits the libations only when they are brought along with the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees that libations brought later are not permitted by the blood. But when they come together with the animal, the blood does permit them, so they can become פיגול. Even so, the dispute stands, and the ending of our ברייתא still matches the רבנן and not רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: I too only said (it in this case)
Libations that come together with the offering

phrases.english: He said to them:
I too did not say it,
except about those that come with the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's objection from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seemed to say the blood permits all libations, even ones brought later.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only meant libations brought together with the offering, but he still holds those can become פיגול.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the ברייתא follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the whole ברייתא follows רבי, who holds the leper's oil is permitted, and so can become פיגול, through its own placements.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי, who says that the leper's לוג of oil is permitted by its own placements. And since its placements permit it, its placements can also make it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge by naming a different תנא, רבי. With רבי, both the beginning and the end of the ברייתא fit one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the oil does not depend on the blood. Its own placements are what permit it, so a wrong intention during those placements makes it פיגול. That explains why the oil is included. The libations are not included, because they have nothing like that which permits them, so the ending fits too.

keyTerms.meaning: Its placements (the seven sprinklings of the oil before ה')
Permit it
Make it פיגול

steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the ברייתא as one consistent opinion. It also shows the rule that whatever permits an item is what can make it פיגול.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name after it means רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is not a general word for 'a rabbi'.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi,
who says: the log of oil of a leper,
its placements permit it;
phrases.notes: This is the oil sprinkled seven times 'before ה'' (ויקרא 14:16), not the אשם's blood.

phrases.english: and since its placements permit it,
its placements make it piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by naming a different תנא than step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to follow רבי מאיר in its beginning and the רבנן in its end.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא follows רבי. The oil can become פיגול through its own placements, and the libations cannot.

steps.title: Source: the oil's מעילה status before and after the blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one is liable for מעילה on the leper's oil until the blood is sprinkled. After that, one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: with the leper's לוג of oil, one is liable for מעילה until the blood is sprinkled. Once the blood is sprinkled, one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as the source for רבי's view about the leper's oil. This first part gives the opposing, unnamed opinion, which ties the oil's status to the sprinkling of the אשם's blood. רבי's own view follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this first opinion, the oil is fully holy before the blood is sprinkled, so using it is מעילה. Once the אשם's blood is sprinkled, מעילה ends, though one still may not use the oil. For this opinion, then, the blood is what releases the oil, and רבי will disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, misusing holy property
Once the blood has been sprinkled
One may not benefit from it

steps.whatToRemember: The first part of the ברייתא fits רבי מאיר, but its ending clashes with him. רב יוסף therefore says the whole ברייתא follows רבי, for whom the leper's oil is permitted, and so can become פיגול, through its own placements.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: The log of oil of a leper:
one is liable for misuse with it,
until he sprinkles the blood.
phrases.notes: This is the blood of the leper's אשם.

phrases.english: Once the blood was sprinkled,
one may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לוֹג שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע – מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבי's view stated in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view about how the leper's oil becomes permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on the oil's מעילה status before and after the blood is sprinkled

steps.title: רבי says the oil's own sprinklings end מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי holds that מעילה on the leper's oil ends once the oil's own sprinklings are done. Everyone agrees the oil may not be eaten until both the seven sprinklings and the placing on the thumb and big toe are done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: one is liable for מעילה until the כהן does the oil's own placements. Both sides agree that eating the oil is forbidden until he does the seven sprinklings and the placing on the thumb and big toe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. Here we hear רבי's opinion, and this opinion is what supports רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the animal's blood is what ends מעילה. רבי says the oil's own seven sprinklings end it. That means, for רבי, the oil has its own מתיר (the thing that makes it permitted), just as blood is the מתיר for meat. Something with its own מתיר can become פיגול through that service, which is exactly what רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: Its own placements, meaning the oil's own sprinklings
The seven sprinklings of oil toward the קודש הקדשים
Placing oil on the leper's right thumb and right big toe
And they agree. Both opinions accept this point
The service that makes an offering permitted, for eating or for the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. מעילה ends after the seven sprinklings alone (according to רבי). Eating is allowed only after the thumb and toe placing is done too. Both sides agree on that second point.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source behind רב יוסף's claim. It shows that for רבי the oil's sprinklings work like blood: they change the oil's status, so they can make it פיגול.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: one is liable for misuse of sacred property
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one רב יוסף said the ברייתא follows.

phrases.english: until he places its placements.
And they agree that it is forbidden to eat
until he places the seven placements
and the placement on the thumbs.
phrases.notes: Literally 'thumbs.' He means the leper's thumb and big toe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: מוֹעֲלִין, עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן מַתְּנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 31 by giving רבי's opposing view, which backs רב יוסף (step 30).
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that, for רבי, the leper's oil is permitted by its own placements and so can become פיגול through them
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: רבי says מעילה applies until the oil's own placements are done

steps.title: רבי ירמיה is shocked by רב יוסף's explanation
steps.stepSummary: When רב יוסף's explanation was repeated before רבי ירמיה, he reacted with amazement: how could a great man like רב יוסף say such a thing?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said this explanation in front of רבי ירמיה. He said: would a great man like רב יוסף say something like this?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה objects to רב יוסף's answer. He is shocked by it. This line sets up an attack, and the גמרא explains what is wrong with it on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are a question, but they work as a challenge. רבי ירמיה is not asking for information. He is saying that רב יוסף's idea, that the oil's sprinklings can make it פיגול, cannot be right. The exact reason for his objection comes on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: They said it before him. Someone repeated a teaching in front of a scholar
A great man, a major scholar
Should he say? Here it is used to show surprise
A thing, a statement

phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Yirmeya,
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב יוסף's explanation from step 30.

phrases.english: he said: a great man like Rav Yosef
should say a thing like this?!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא רַבָּא כְּרַב יוֹסֵף, לֵימָא כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא seemed to support רב יוסף, רבי ירמיה rejects his explanation with surprise.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's explanation that the ברייתא follows רבי, so the leper's oil can become פיגול through its own placements
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A cry of astonishment. רבי ירמיה claims the idea is so plainly wrong that a great scholar should not have said it. The detailed reason follows in the next part of the גמרא.
